title: Learning from Revision Consequences: Hindsight Meta-Experience Distillation for Self-Improving Agents
title_zh: 从修订后果中学习：面向自我改进智能体的事后元经验蒸馏
abstract_en: As agents continuously improve by generating and revising Skills, the process that discovers and refines those Skills becomes a learnable object in its own right. Task-Skills directly act on task execution, whereas Meta-Skills govern how agents discover and improve future Skills; their value therefore emerges through the subsequent search processes they induce. Existing approaches improve Meta-Skills from observed raw Skill-search trajectories and branch outcomes. However, branch performance entangles the effects of the initial discovery state and the Meta-Skill revision that generated the search process, making it difficult to characterize what a particular revision actually changed, and pushing updates toward revisions that benefit from favorable states rather than those that improve the process. We introduce HMED (Hindsight Meta-Experience Distillation), a mechanism for constructing Meta-Experience for self-improving agents. HMED revisits the completed event from which a revision originates and re-executes the incumbent and revised Meta-Skills from the same restored discovery state, so that the changes associated with the revision can be observed under a shared condition. Each comparison is distilled into a Meta-Experience, a structured record that can be reused by future updates, so that even revisions that are not ultimately retained still contribute a learning signal. Across three interactive agent benchmarks and both open-source and closed-source models, HMED consistently improves Skill discovery performance over strong baselines, shifting Meta-Skill learning beyond branch outcomes toward the consequences of changing the improvement process.
abstract_zh: 智能体通过生成和修订 Skills 持续改进，而发现与优化这些 Skills 的过程本身也可以成为学习对象。Task-Skills 直接执行任务，Meta-Skills 则决定智能体如何发现和改进未来的 Skills，其价值体现在后续搜索过程中。现有方法通常依据原始 Skill 搜索轨迹及分支结果来优化 Meta-Skills，但分支表现同时受到初始发现状态和 Meta-Skill 修订的影响，难以判断某次修订究竟带来了什么变化，容易偏向有利初始状态，而非真正改善搜索过程。本文提出 HMED（Hindsight Meta-Experience Distillation），用于构建自我改进智能体的 Meta-Experience。HMED 回溯产生某次修订的已完成事件，恢复到相同的发现状态，并分别重新执行当前版本与修订后的 Meta-Skills，从共享条件下直接观测修订造成的差异。每次比较都会被蒸馏为结构化的 Meta-Experience，供后续更新复用，因此即使某次修订最终未被保留，也能提供学习信号。在三个交互式智能体基准以及开源和闭源模型上，HMED 均稳定提升了 Skill 发现性能，使 Meta-Skill 学习从依赖分支结果转向学习改进过程本身所产生的后果。
key_points_zh: 核心问题是解耦初始发现状态与 Meta-Skill 修订对搜索结果的影响。
HMED 在同一恢复后的发现状态下重执行 incumbent 与 revised Meta-Skills，进行公平对比。
对比结果被整理为可复用的结构化 Meta-Experience，未被采纳的修订也能贡献训练信号。
在三个交互式智能体基准及开源、闭源模型上，HMED consistently 提升 Skill discovery 性能。
方法推动 Meta-Skill 学习从拟合分支结果转向学习修订对改进过程的实际影响。

llm_assessment.comment: HMED makes Skill-improvement processes learnable through matched-state counterfactual revision traces, enabling a strong and reusable self-improvement loop.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: HMED通过匹配状态下的反事实修订轨迹使技能改进过程可学习，形成了强而可复用的自我改进闭环。
